                    ### Question
                    Shortly after delivery, a female newborn develops bluish discoloration of the lips, fingers, and toes. She was born at term to a 38-year-old primigravid woman. Pregnancy was complicated by maternal diabetes mellitus. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 81%. Echocardiography shows immediate bifurcation of the vessel arising from the left ventricle; the vessel emerging from the right ventricle gives out coronary, head, and neck vessels. An abnormality in which of the following developmental processes most likely accounts for this patient's condition?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Separation of tricuspid valve tissue from myocardium
opb. Fusion of endocardial cushion
opc. Alignment of infundibular septum
opd. Division of aorta and pulmonary artery
ope. Spiraling of aorticopulmonary septum

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The abnormal vessel arising from the left ventricle in the newborn most likely results from the division of the aorta and pulmonary artery during development. Maternal diabetes mellitus increases the risk of congenital heart defects, and in this case, the abnormal vessel distribution is consistent with the division of aorta and pulmonary artery. The evidence paths support the involvement of blood vessels and left ventricular structures in cardiac development.
